<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Wire the tree-sitter TypeScript and TSX grammars into fs3-parsers so .ts/.tsx files stop being bare file elements (backlog row 147: every TypeScript file in the index today is one unparsed blob — the pij extensions, this repo's own tooling, and most of the fleet's code). The extraction walk is generic; the packet is the two Language entries, the grammar crate, the classify decisions for TypeScript node kinds, a generic value-shape rule so arrow-function bindings (the dominant TS style) become Function elements, fixtures with golden element forests, and a real-usage receipt on prod after re-ingest.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- `.ts`/`.mts`/`.cts` → Language::TypeScript, `.tsx` → Language::Tsx; file subkind reports the language
- functions, classes (incl. abstract), interfaces, enums, type aliases, methods, method/function signatures and namespaces become named elements with correct addresses and spans
- arrow-function / function-expression bindings (`const f = () => {}`, `export const h = async () => {}`, class-field arrows) become Function elements named by their binding, via a language-agnostic value-shape rule in the generic walk
- golden fixture tests for every decision, including the deliberate non-elements, with mutation receipts
- prod receipt: after re-ingest of a TS-heavy repo, `flowspace3 search` returns TS function/container elements, not bare files

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- JavaScript/JSX (`.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`) — separate packet; tree-sitter-javascript is a different crate
- changing ElementKind, the store schema, embeddings, or any CLI envelope
- decorators, overload merging, declaration-merging semantics beyond what the generic walk yields
- re-ingesting prod yourself — o-prime does the prod re-ingest and takes the receipt
